confounds.name: Benchmark over-optimization rather than broader math reasoning
confounds.detail: The paper notes that widely used benchmarks such as MATH, GSM8K, and AIME may risk over-optimization, which could make strong scores appear to show general reasoning ability.
confounds.ruled_out_by: It also reports results on Olympiad Bench, College Math, and the out-of-domain Gaokao En 2023 benchmark, and states that the training set was not specifically optimized for them.

confounds.name: More test-time samples, rather than the method, explain the advantage over Best-of-N
confounds.detail: A higher number of sampled solutions could by itself improve accuracy relative to a baseline using fewer samples.
confounds.ruled_out_by: For the Qwen Best-of-N comparison, the paper says rStar-Math generates the same number of solutions as Qwen.

confounds.name: Unsolved synthetic problems reflect incorrect labels rather than insufficient model reasoning
confounds.detail: The remaining unsolved problems after self-evolution could be invalid questions or have wrong ground-truth answers, rather than being valid hard problems the models cannot solve.
confounds.ruled_out_by: The authors manually reviewed a random sample of 20 remaining problems and found that 19 had incorrect labels with wrong answers.

confounds.name: Correct final answers can conceal flawed intermediate reasoning
confounds.detail: A trajectory could reach a correct answer by chance while containing incorrect or irrelevant intermediate steps, so answer accuracy alone would not establish the claimed quality of the training trajectories.
confounds.ruled_out_by: During code-augmented CoT generation, the paper retains only candidates whose concatenated Python code executes successfully, and uses MCTS rollouts to annotate and select steps and trajectories.

evidence_standards.name: Reported test-time decoding and trajectory counts
evidence_standards.detail: The paper reports Pass@1 accuracy with 16 trajectories for AIME and AMC and 8 for other benchmarks, uses the PPM to select the best solution, and additionally reports rStar-Math64 with 64 trajectories. System 2 baselines use default evaluation settings, including default thinking time for o1-preview and o1-mini. The paper does not report a statistical test, seed-based variance, confidence intervals, or a threshold for treating differences as real.

metrics.name: robust accuracy
metrics.caveat: Attack-based evaluation gives an upper bound on robust accuracy and can overestimate it if attacks are ineffective; the paper reports AutoAttack results and, when available, the lowest robust accuracy from AutoAttack and other evaluations, and encourages adaptive or external attacks.

metrics.name: expected calibration error (ECE)

metrics.name: relative standard deviation (RSD) of robust accuracy over classes
membership inference accuracy
metrics.caveat: Inference accuracy based on confidence is not much higher than the baseline determined by the generalization gap; the paper reports the generalization gap alongside membership inference accuracy.

controls.name: standard model
controls.detail: The paper compares robustly trained models with a standard, non-robustly trained model in analyses including calibration, OOD detection, and privacy leakage.
controls.rules_out: A difference against this reference establishes how the reported property differs from the standard-model reference; it does not by itself isolate a particular mechanism of robust training.

confounds.name: apparent robustness is caused by ineffective attacks rather than actual robustness
confounds.detail: An attack may fail to find adversarial examples, making the reported robust accuracy too high; the paper notes that black-box attacks outperforming white-box attacks can indicate this problem.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Evaluate with AutoAttack’s white- and black-box attack ensemble; flag evaluations when Square Attack lowers robust accuracy by more than 0.2% relative to the white-box attacks, and use or encourage adaptive evaluations for potentially unreliable cases.

confounds.name: privacy leakage reflects the generalization gap rather than a specific effect of robust training
confounds.detail: Membership inference accuracy could be explained by the generalization gap, so it would not establish that robust training itself causes greater leakage.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Compare confidence-based membership inference accuracy with the baseline determined by the generalization gap and report the generalization gap alongside inference accuracy.

evidence_standards.name: AutoAttack reliability flag
evidence_standards.detail: The paper flags a model when Square Attack reduces robust accuracy by more than 0.2% compared with the white-box gradient-based attacks in AutoAttack; it treats the evaluation as potentially unreliable and adaptive attacks as potentially necessary.

evidence_standards.name: independent standardized evaluation
evidence_standards.detail: The paper performs the standardized evaluation independently of the authors of submitted models to support reproducibility. It also reports AutoAttack variability over random seeds, but the provided text does not state the number of seeds or a statistical test.

metrics.name: Task 1 true positive rate (TPR)
metrics.caveat: Reported alongside TNR and MCC for solution-correctness classification; the paper notes that few-shot prompting can raise TPR while lowering TNR, so TPR alone does not show the full effect.

metrics.name: Task 1 true negative rate (TNR)
metrics.caveat: Reported alongside TPR and MCC for solution-correctness classification; the paper notes that few-shot prompting can lower TNR while raising TPR, so TNR alone does not show the full effect.

metrics.name: Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC)
metrics.caveat: The paper treats negative MCC as no better than random and clips it to zero in MR-Score; zero is the normalization cutoff.

metrics.name: Task 2 accuracy (first-error-step accuracy)
metrics.caveat: Calculated over incorrect solutions; the paper does not state a separate caveat.

metrics.name: Task 3 accuracy (first-error-step and error-reason accuracy)
metrics.caveat: Calculated over incorrect solutions; error reasons are examined only after the model correctly identifies an incorrect solution and its first-error-step.

metrics.name: MR-Score
metrics.caveat: A weighted combination of clipped MCC, first-error-step accuracy, and error-reason accuracy. The weights are chosen empirically to maximize differentiation between model performances, accounting for task difficulty.

controls.name: Zero-shot condition (k=0)
controls.detail: The paper compares the three-demonstration condition (k=3) with evaluation without demonstrations, using the same inference temperature of 0.
controls.rules_out: Shows whether observed few-shot results differ from performance without demonstrations.

controls.name: Few-shot demonstration-composition ablation
controls.detail: The paper varies the number of correct solutions in the three-shot demonstrations; the standard examples contain two correct solutions and one incorrect solution. The paper reports the resulting TPR and TNR changes in Figure 6.
controls.rules_out: Tests whether few-shot changes in correctness judgments are associated with the correctness distribution of the demonstrations, rather than only with adding demonstrations.

confounds.name: Few-shot results reflect bias from the correctness distribution in the demonstrations, rather than reasoning about the solutions
confounds.detail: The three-shot examples contain two correct and one incorrect solution, which could sway models toward particular correctness judgments and help explain the TPR/TNR shifts and weaker few-shot results.
confounds.ruled_out_by: The authors vary the number of correct solutions in the three-shot demonstrations and measure TPR and TNR; they report a strong correlation between demonstration composition and the observed shifts.

evidence_standards.name: Inference temperature 0; results reported for k=0 and k=3
evidence_standards.detail: The paper says temperature 0 is used across models to minimize variance and reports zero-shot and three-shot results. It reports no seeds, variance estimates, statistical tests, or significance threshold for deciding whether model differences are real.

datasets.name: LRBENCH
datasets.eval_protocol: Evaluate on the 300-case test split, evenly sampled across medical, legal, and academic domains, using an identical prompt for all models. Report accuracy overall, by domain, and by principle. The dataset is split into 104,990 training instances and 300 test instances; candidate order is randomized during dataset construction.

datasets.name: RewardBench (Chat Hard subset)
datasets.eval_protocol: Evaluate on 456 pairs, subdividing Chat Hard into six applications following the RewardBench taxonomy; report accuracy for each application. Use the same prompt for all compared methods.

datasets.name: JudgeBench (Reasoning subset)
datasets.eval_protocol: Evaluate on the 98 examples with explicit reasoning chains in the Reasoning subset; report accuracy. Use the same prompt for all compared methods.

metrics.name: Pairwise comparison accuracy
metrics.caveat: Binary preference judgments can miss fine-grained reasoning defects; the paper also reports principle-level accuracy.

controls.name: Qwen3-8B base model
controls.detail: The unmodified backbone is evaluated alongside models post-trained on LRBENCH.
controls.rules_out: Whether the trained-model result is already present in the base model, rather than arising after LRBENCH post-training.

controls.name: Judge-R1-fc
controls.detail: Full context only; no SFT warm-up and no search.
controls.rules_out: Provides the no-warm-up/no-search reference for comparisons with warm-up and search variants.

controls.name: Judge-R1-warm-fc
controls.detail: Lightweight SFT warm-up plus full context; no search.
controls.rules_out: Compared with the full model, tests whether the result depends on adding multi-turn search when warm-up and full context are present.

controls.name: Judge-R1-search
controls.detail: Search-only; no warm-up and no full context.
controls.rules_out: Compared with the full-context-only variant, tests the contribution of multi-turn search rather than static full-context concatenation.

controls.name: Judge-R1-fc-search
controls.detail: Full context plus multi-turn search; no warm-up.
controls.rules_out: Compared with the full model, tests whether the result depends on adding the SFT warm-up when full context and search are present.

confounds.name: OOD gains could come from shortcut learning rather than genuine judgment learning
confounds.detail: The models might exploit superficial input cues to obtain higher benchmark accuracy without using the evaluation principles or case-specific evidence.
confounds.ruled_out_by: The paper analyzes attention patterns, reasoning traces, and class bias: GRPO-8B places over 90% of decision-token attention on the principle section, more often cites case-specific evidence than the base model, and has lower class bias. The authors report no evidence that OOD gains are driven by shortcut learning.

confounds.name: Retrieval gains could reflect irrelevant or out-of-case passages rather than useful case-grounded evidence
confounds.detail: A retrieval model might appear to benefit from search while retrieving passages unrelated to the particular judgment case.
confounds.ruled_out_by: With matched rollout settings and the same case-context corpus, 79.93% of passages retrieved by Search-R1-7B came from outside the target case; Judge-R1 restricts retrieval to the current case.

confounds.name: Synthetic flawed reasonings may not represent natural reasoning errors
confounds.detail: Because LRBENCH’s flawed reasonings are generated using Claude-3.7-Sonnet, results on the benchmark may not capture performance on the diversity of errors produced by models in real-world settings.

Evaluated on the test set using classification, report-generation, and structural-consistency metrics.

baselines.name: NetMamba
baselines.fair_comparison: Evaluated on the same preprocessed test sets; the paper reports its linear-head Accuracy, while generative methods’ classification is scored as JSON Classification Accuracy extracted from their reports.

baselines.name: Zero-shot LLM
baselines.fair_comparison: Evaluated on the same preprocessed test sets; defined as feeding features directly to the LLM without tuning. Generative-method classification is scored by extracting the class from the generated report.

baselines.name: Vanilla
baselines.fair_comparison: Evaluated on the same preprocessed test sets; defined as freezing the encoder without auxiliary constraints. Generative-method classification is scored by extracting the class from the generated report.

metrics.name: ROUGE-L
metrics.caveat: Reference-based scores can be insensitive to classification correctness because category descriptions share protocol-level vocabulary. The paper reports classification accuracy and reference-free structural metrics (ETC, QCR, PMR) alongside it.

metrics.name: BERTScore
metrics.caveat: Reference-based scores can be insensitive to classification correctness because category descriptions share protocol-level vocabulary. The paper reports classification accuracy and reference-free structural metrics (ETC, QCR, PMR) alongside it; BERTScore is described as more robust than ROUGE-L to lexical paraphrasing and stylistic variation.

controls.name: V1 (Vanilla MLLM)
controls.detail: Ablation condition with the NetMamba encoder frozen and standard negative log-likelihood loss only; evaluated in the ablation study on ISCX-Tor-2016 and ISCXVPN2016.
controls.rules_out: Comparing V2 with V1 tests whether unfreezing the encoder contributes beyond the frozen-encoder condition.

controls.name: V2 (+ Unfrozen)
controls.detail: Unfreezes the traffic encoder for end-to-end joint optimization, without the auxiliary classification head or semantic-priority generation loss; evaluated on ISCX-Tor-2016 and ISCXVPN2016.
controls.rules_out: Comparing V3 with V2 tests the contribution of adding the auxiliary classification head after unfreezing the encoder.

controls.name: V3 (+ Auxiliary Head)
controls.detail: Adds the auxiliary classification head to V2, but does not include the semantic-priority guided generation mechanism; evaluated on ISCX-Tor-2016 and ISCXVPN2016.
controls.rules_out: Comparing V4 with V3 tests the contribution of semantic-priority guided generation beyond the auxiliary-head condition.

confounds.name: Reference-based text scores can look good despite incorrect traffic classification
confounds.detail: Shared protocol-level vocabulary across category descriptions may let a model obtain moderate ROUGE-L or BERTScore while misidentifying the traffic, the paper’s “fluency trap.”
confounds.ruled_out_by: The paper reports classification accuracy (including JSON Classification Accuracy for generative models) and reference-free structural metrics ETC, QCR, and PMR alongside reference-based text scores.
